items.headline: Suspected Chinese APT rebuilds EggStreme malware after exposure; Philippine government targeted
items.summary: Bitdefender reports a suspected Chinese APT rebuilt its EggStreme Windows malware framework after its September 2025 disclosure, with a passive backdoor and new protocol, while still targeting Philippine government organizations.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Single vendor research update; victims unnamed, attribution unconfirmed by authorities.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (Bitdefender blog date; time not stated); first coverage 18 Nov 2026 via Infosecurity Magazine and The Hacker News

sections.happened: Bitdefender published an update on 18 November 2026 to its EggStreme research first published in September 2025. It assessed with high confidence that the suspected Chinese APT operation continues to target multiple Philippine government organizations, and with low to medium confidence that Taiwan is targeted. It said the timing suggests its report was a likely trigger for the rebuild. It made no new attribution claim.
sections.technical: Fuel configuration protection changed 12 days after the report; the loader moved from RC4 to RC5 then a custom cipher by late October 2025. The agent switched to raw TCP with mutual TLS, dropped the keylogger, added AD and WMI recon and in-memory PowerShell, and has passive builds that listen rather than beacon. DLL sideloading, SMB file-share movement and in-memory execution persist. No CVE involved; initial access unknown.
sections.guidance: Bitdefender recommends restricting built-in Windows tools an environment does not need, detecting DLL sideloading by library name and location, finding unmanaged machines that can reach workstations, and watching for new inbound listeners on workstations.
sections.differing: Bitdefender assesses Taiwan targeting only at low to medium confidence and calls it a lead. Palo Alto Networks tracks CL-STA-1048 using EggStremeFuel and Loader from March to September 2025; Bitdefender says it has not compared infrastructure or victims to determine whether they are the same cluster.
sections.unknown: Initial access vector is unknown. Victim organizations and counts are not named. Whether EggStremeWizard is still deployed, and whether the keylogger was retired, remain unestablished.

items.headline: Equinor confirms ongoing cyberattack on IT systems; production unaffected
items.summary: Equinor says an ongoing cyber-attack hit certain IT systems; production is running normally and no data theft is indicated. Attribution and entry point are undisclosed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Equinor's own statements; no attribution or technical detail published.
items.firstReported: 17:55 GMT (18:55 CET), 17 November 2026, Equinor statement on equinor.com

sections.happened: On 17 November 2026 Equinor said it had detected an ongoing cyber-attack against certain IT systems. Its 19 November update says the attack is still ongoing, production is running as normal, and no data theft or alteration is indicated. Police and national security authorities have been informed.
sections.technical: Equinor says the attack is not a virus, so there is no risk of it spreading. Initial access, vector, affected systems and any malware are undisclosed. No MITRE ATT&CK or CVE mapping has been published.

sections.differing: Equinor says it still has access to its systems (spokesperson, via NTB). An unnamed Equinor source told Reuters the internal email system was down.
sections.unknown: Entry point, full scope, whether operational technology was reached, attribution and recovery timeline. Equinor says it is too early to say.

items.headline: N-able confirms unauthorised server access disrupts Mail Assure and SpamExperts management
items.summary: N-able confirms unauthorised access to one server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud. Portal, APIs, quarantine and logging are offline in three regions; mail flow continues.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Vendor (N-able) acknowledged unauthorised server access; no data compromise found so far. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026 (customer disruption notice, time not stated); The Hacker News 19 Nov 2026

sections.happened: N-able began investigating a service disruption to Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud on 16 Nov 2026, first attributed to configuration. On 18 Nov it said one server had unauthorised access. Management portal, APIs, quarantine and logging are offline across Americas, APAC and Europe. Mail flow continues. Restoration was ongoing at 08:00 UTC on 19 Nov.
sections.technical: Unauthorised access to one server in the hosted cloud. Attacker, entry method and dwell time not disclosed. No CVE or ATT&CK mapping published. Stated as unrelated to the N-central vulnerabilities (Able2Shell and related names).
sections.guidance: N-able says it emailed partners with environment-specific information on whether action is required. Partners not receiving it should contact N-able Technical Support.
sections.differing: N-able's 17 Nov update attributed the disruption to configuration and dependencies; the 18 Nov update revised this to a security incident. Earlier account is superseded.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, access method, duration, and whether credentials were exposed remain unconfirmed. Restoration timeline not given. Investigation ongoing.

items.headline: Rakuten Securities reports test-environment breach affecting up to 15.72 million accounts
items.summary: Rakuten Securities says unauthorised access to a test environment holding real customer data may have exposed login IDs for 11.25 million accounts and fuller personal and financial details for 4.47 million. Passwords and PINs reportedly were not taken.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Company disclosure reported consistently by multiple independent outlets; investigation ongoing. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (Japan time), Rakuten Securities notice, as reported by Infosecurity Magazine and Japan Times

sections.happened: Rakuten Securities, Rakuten Group's online brokerage, announced on 17 November that it detected possible unauthorised access on 16 November and blocked access. It later found information in a test environment may have been taken on 11 November. Up to 15.72 million accounts, including closed ones, are potentially affected: 11.25 million with branch/customer codes and login IDs, and 4.47 million with names, addresses, contact details, bank details, income and asset data. The company says no passwords or PINs were taken and no unauthorised logins or trades have been seen. Rakuten Group shares fell over 7% on 18 November; the firm postponed a Shibuya store opening and waived fund-transfer fees.
sections.technical: The test environment normally uses dummy data, but real production customer data was copied in to verify an internal system update, according to a company spokesperson quoted by ASCII.jp. Access occurred while that data was present. Initial vector, actor and malware are undisclosed; one aggregator claims an exploited vulnerability, unverified. No CVE or IOCs published. The company is investigating cause with outside parties.
sections.guidance: Rakuten Securities warned of phishing emails, texts, calls and letters impersonating it, and said its emails contain no links. It is making passkey login mandatory, urged customers without passkeys to set one up, and pointed to a self-service trading and withdrawal suspension setting.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, entry method, whether data was actually exfiltrated or published, and the reason real data was in the test environment beyond a system update remain undisclosed. Investigation is continuing.

items.headline: TfL takes Oyster photocard site offline after account compromise affecting about 265,000 customers
items.summary: Transport for London took its Oyster photocard website offline on 16 November after customers received unexpected account-creation emails. TfL says about 265,000 accounts may be compromised, no passwords or payment data, and has notified the ICO. Entry method undisclosed.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: TfL statement via The Register, Infosecurity Magazine and ianVisits; ICO notified. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026 11:01 GMT, The Register (TfL became aware 16 Nov)

sections.happened: On 16 November 2026 Oyster photocard customers received emails from TfL's own systems asking them to create accounts they already held. TfL took the photocard website down and says about 265,000 customers may have had account details compromised. Affected card types include Zip Oyster, 18+ Student, 60+ London, Apprentice, Care Leaver and Veterans photocards. TfL says it has contained the incident, contacted affected customers and notified the Information Commissioner's Office. Existing photocards still work at barriers; renewals and journey-history queries go through customer services. The site remained offline at time of reporting.
sections.technical: TfL has not disclosed how attackers gained access. It said the emails were generated by its systems as a result of the compromise. It reports no passwords, bank or payment card details or journey data were accessed, and believes children's names and dates of birth were unaffected. One outlet reports contact details, dates of birth and security answers may be exposed. No CVE, actor, malware or IOCs published.
sections.guidance: TfL says it will ask all photocard customers to change their password, security question and answer, and advises changing the password on any other service where it was reused. Customers needing renewals or journey history can call TfL customer services.
sections.differing: TfL says no passwords were accessed, yet it is asking all customers to reset passwords. Reports differ on exposed fields: TfL statements cited stress what was not taken; ianVisits lists contact details, dates of birth and security answers.
sections.unknown: Entry vector, attacker identity, exact data fields taken, and website restoration date are undisclosed. TfL says nothing indicates a link to the 2024 attack.

items.firstReported: Nov 19 2026, 04:23 AM ET (BleepingComputer); listing posted Nov 18 2026

Nvidia told BleepingComputer it is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner and found no sign its systems were affected.

items.headline: Microsoft agent-framework PyPI releases 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 carried credential stealer
items.summary: Two malicious agent-framework releases appeared on PyPI on 17 November 2026 with a .pth startup hook that harvests cloud and CI/CD credentials. PyPI quarantined both. Microsoft's repository says they were not built from it; 1.26.0 is the last clean version.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Maintainer repo issue plus StepSecurity analysis, Help Net Security reporting; PyPI removed versions
items.firstReported: 2026-11-17 21:35 UTC (same as UK time, GMT): Upwind Security report on microsoft/agent-framework GitHub issue #10411

sections.happened: Version 1.26.1 of the agent-framework package was uploaded to PyPI at 20:35 UTC on 17 November 2026 and quarantined at 21:06 UTC. Version 1.26.2 followed at 21:08 UTC and was quarantined at 21:16 UTC. The Microsoft repository issue, reported by Upwind Security, says the release was uploaded outside the project's release pipeline, most likely with a compromised upload credential. OX Security put the package at 192,534 monthly downloads. Initial access has not been explained.
sections.technical: A .pth file runs on every Python interpreter start, with no import of the framework needed. The payload collects environment variables matching strings such as TOKEN, SECRET, AZURE, AWS and GITHUB, credential files, and other processes' environments via /proc. StepSecurity says it requests GitHub Actions OIDC, Azure DevOps OIDC and Azure managed-identity tokens, then sends data to a webhook.site endpoint. Version 1.26.2 moved the hook to af_runtime_diag.pth.
sections.guidance: Microsoft's issue says to pin agent-framework==1.26.0 and not rely on upgrading to latest. StepSecurity says to isolate affected environments before running Python or pip, rebuild from a clean base, audit egress logs for webhook.site and review OIDC and managed-identity permissions.
sections.unknown: How the attacker obtained publishing access, whether that credential is revoked, whether any tokens were issued, and how many environments installed the releases remain unconfirmed.

items.headline: Optimizely flaw used to inject malicious JavaScript into 178+ major websites
items.summary: On 16 November an attacker abused Optimizely's account signup flow to inject card-skimming, crypto-swapping and iOS exploit-kit JavaScript into customer scripts, affecting at least 178 organisations including BBC, CNN and Zoom. Optimizely says it is fixed and Mandiant is investigating.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Optimizely acknowledged incident; researcher and multiple outlets corroborate. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 16 Nov 2026 (UK, approx. 04:21 GMT first injection per iTnews AEDT time); public report by Report URI/Scott Helme, 16–17 Nov

sections.happened: Report URI's Scott Helme reported that on 16 November malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organisations via Optimizely's platform, including BBC, CNN, Equifax, Ledger and Zoom. iTnews put the first injection at 3:21pm AEDT Monday, with most scripts cleaned by about 8:10am Tuesday. Optimizely confirmed an unauthorised party exploited a vulnerability and said it has fully remediated it. TPG Telecom paused Optimizely on Vodafone Australia pages; iTnews understands HSBC disabled it globally.
sections.technical: Optimizely told customers the attacker created accounts via the Experimentation signup flow, then exploited a flaw to act as existing administrators, guessing staff email variations up to thousands of times per customer. Injected code in customer projects was served from Optimizely's script host. The payload was rebuilt 26 times, adding a skimmer for cards, cookies and screenshots, crypto-address swapping, and redirection of older iPhones and iPads to the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits. Helme traced about US$7040 to attacker wallets. No CVE was cited.
sections.guidance: Helme advised iPhone and iPad users to update to iOS 18.7.3 or 26.3 or later, and card payers on affected sites on 16 November to monitor statements. Report URI said 24 affected sites had CSPs that fully blocked the payload. TPG advised iOS 18.6 or earlier users to update.
sections.differing: Helme's first injection (3:21pm AEDT) precedes Optimizely's report of the first malicious code written at 6:51pm AEDT. Optimizely says Cloudflare delivery was blocked at 3:06am Tuesday; StepSecurity scan data suggest requests continued until about 8:23am. Helme counted 188 infected scripts among 1611 checked.
sections.unknown: Number of cards, cookies and screenshots captured is unknown; Optimizely can see only code loads, not captured data. Attacker identity is unattributed. Mandiant's investigation is ongoing.

items.headline: Apache confirms exploitation of unauthenticated Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE (CVE-2026-129448)
items.summary: The Apache Software Foundation says CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated deserialization flaw in Apache Roller's XML-RPC endpoint, is being actively exploited. Versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 are affected; 6.1.6 or later fixes it. No attack details published.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: ASF advisory states active exploitation; no attack details or actor given. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 17 Nov 2026 (ASF advisory per SecurityWeek); first article read: The Hacker News, 18 Nov 2026

sections.happened: The Apache Software Foundation published an advisory on 17 November 2026 stating that CVE-2026-129448, a CVSS 9.8 flaw in the Java blogging platform Apache Roller, is being actively exploited. It is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, disclosed in September with only Roller 6.1.5 listed as affected; the new notice widens the range to 4.0.0 through 6.1.4. The researcher n0mi1k is credited with finding it and Matt Raible with reporting it. Roller 6.1.7, released 11 November, fixes another 15 vulnerabilities, per SecurityWeek.
sections.technical: The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester (unsafe deserialization, CWE-502), allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Affected: 4.0.0 through 6.1.4. Fixed: 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the feature is disabled. Disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI does not prevent exploitation on older versions. No IOCs, actor or malware published.
sections.guidance: ASF advises upgrading to Roller 6.1.6 or later. If that is not possible, set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, then restart Roller. ASF says disabling XML-RPC in the admin UI is not enough.
sections.differing: The September advisory (CVE-2026-82384) listed only 6.1.5 as affected; the November notice says the same flaw affects 4.0.0 through 6.1.4. The later notice is the broader and current scope.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, number of victims, exploitation techniques, targeted sectors, and whether a CISA KEV listing exists for this CVE are not published.

items.headline: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 exploited against Russian organisation after public PoC, F6 says
items.summary: F6 reports attackers used critical Cisco Expressway flaw CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8) to breach a Russian organisation shortly after a GitHub PoC appeared. Cisco's advisory, published 21 October, had not been revised to mention exploitation.
items.label: VENDOR-ACKNOWLEDGED
items.labelBasis: Cisco confirmed the flaw and fix; exploitation rests on F6 via SecurityWeek.
items.firstReported: Advisory 21 Oct 2026 17:00 BST, Cisco; exploitation report via SecurityWeek

sections.happened: Cisco published an advisory on 21 October 2026 for CVE-2026-76466, a critical flaw in Expressway Core and Edge. A proof-of-concept exploit was later posted on GitHub. Security firm F6 says attackers then breached an unnamed Russian organisation via two internet-exposed Expressway X15.5.3 devices, pivoting to two internal cluster nodes. SecurityWeek says the Cisco advisory had not been revised and still stated Cisco knew of no malicious use. SecurityWeek asked Cisco for comment.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 9.8, CWE-798) lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run commands as root. It affects clustered devices. Cause: persistent cookies plus unvalidated client certificates in the database service. An attacker holding the cookies can send RPC commands. F6 reports custom Python scripts for network scanning, SMB, SQL Server, WinRM and GitLab searching, edited during the attack, with comments suggesting AI assistant use. Detection is via the Erlang system log. No actor was attributed.
sections.guidance: Cisco: Expressway X15.5.20 fixes the flaw; no workarounds exist, and X14 or earlier users must migrate to a fixed release. F6 recommends, where patching is not possible, blocking TCP 4371–4372 except from trusted cluster nodes.
sections.differing: Cisco's advisory says no workarounds exist, while F6 suggests blocking TCP ports 4371–4372 as a stopgap. Exploitation claims come from F6 only.
sections.unknown: The victim, the actor, the PoC's author and exploitation scale are unknown. Cisco's response to F6's findings is unknown.

items.headline: Java4Shell: critical OpenJDK Base64 flaw (CVE-2026-114938) draws exploitation attempts; CISA urges patching
items.summary: Calif disclosed CVE-2026-114938, an OpenJDK Base64 decoder memory-corruption flaw, on 17 November. Oracle and OpenJDK shipped patches. Scanning and blind exploitation attempts are reported; compromise is unconfirmed. Exploitation needs x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Researcher, Oracle patches, CISA and multiple vendors acknowledged; probing seen by several firms.
items.firstReported: 17 November 2026 (time not stated), Calif write-up calif.io/java4shell

sections.happened: Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) on 17 November, after some details leaked before coordinated disclosure, per Infosecurity Magazine. Oracle and OpenJDK released patches the same day and CISA issued an alert. Calif says it achieved unauthenticated RCE in default Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Keycloak and others, each needing a tailored chain. By early 19 November GreyNoise logged over 150 matching requests from five IPs, WatchTowr saw spraying, and Previdian logged nine attempts; none confirmed successful. Cisco, Siemens, Elastic, Red Hat and Atlassian have published advisories; some fixes are pending.
sections.technical: Out-of-bounds heap write in OpenJDK's AVX-512 VBMI-accelerated Base64 decoder; a stray '=' yields a negative length and a 64-byte write past a 50-byte array (Calif). Affects OpenJDK 17.0.6 and newer, per SecurityWeek, including 17, 21, 25 and 27. Requires x86-64 with AVX-512 VBMI; ARM is unaffected. CVSS 8.1 (v3.1, Oracle); 9.2 (v4.0, Calif). Calif's public PoC triggers corruption only; VulnCheck has a customer RCE exploit. Elasticsearch RCE needs credentials; unauthenticated gives DoS. No ATT&CK IDs or IOCs published beyond 'java4shell-recon' User-Agents.
sections.guidance: CISA: inventory JDKs, including bundled ones; patch, prioritising internet-facing systems; where unpatched, validate and restrict Base64 input, enforce size limits, limit unauthenticated access; monitor for rogue runtimes and JVM crashes. Atlassian suggests disabling AVX-512 for Data Center products; Jenkins advises updating Java and restarting.
sections.differing: Oracle rates it 8.1 High (CVSS 3.1); Calif rates it 9.2 Critical (CVSS 4.0). VulnCheck and Endor Labs stress hardware-specific, hard exploitation; Calif reports multi-product RCE.
sections.unknown: Whether any exploitation attempt has compromised a system is unconfirmed. Fix timing for Cisco, Siemens, Atlassian Data Center and other vendors is unclear. The leak's source is unstated.

items.headline: F5 patches five critical NGINX flaws (nginx2root); public PoCs available, no exploitation reported
items.summary: F5 fixed five NGINX flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2 on 18 November 2026, led by CVE-2026-123007, an HTTP/2 heap overflow present since 1.9.5. Code execution needs ASLR disabled or bypassed. Public PoCs exist; no in-the-wild exploitation is reported.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: F5 advisories and nginx.org confirm; multiple independent outlets and researchers corroborate. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (UK time not stated), F5/nginx.org advisories; The Hacker News

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 F5 released NGINX Open Source 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, fixing five flaws collectively named nginx2root. All are scored 9.2 on CVSS 4.0. The headline flaw, CVE-2026-123007, is an HTTP/2 flaw present since 1.9.5 (2015). It was reported independently by several parties including Wiz, Rapid7 and Xint. Rapid7 and Censys published proof-of-concept code. Xint chained it with a Linux kernel SCTP bug to reach root. Censys estimates about 9 million affected services with HTTP/2 on. No exploitation has been reported.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-123007: HTTP/2 flow-control flaw (Rapid7: integer underflow) causing heap buffer overflow; F5 says code execution requires ASLR disabled or bypassed. CVE-2026-123633: HTTP/2 use-after-free. CVE-2026-123634: resolver use-after-free needing variable-built proxied names plus SSI or mirror subrequests. CVE-2026-121810: HTTP/3 use-after-free. CVE-2026-113425: mail proxy. Vulnerable: open source 1.9.5 to 1.31.8; Plus 37.x and R34 to R36. Code runs with worker privileges; root needs a separate kernel bug. Rapid7's exploit needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic.
sections.guidance: F5 lists upgrading to the fixed versions. Per The Hacker News, F5 gives workarounds for only two flaws (avoid SSI/mirror with variable server names; restrict mail proxy listeners), and CIRCL suggests disabling HTTP/2 temporarily and restarting fully, since a reload keeps the old binary.
sections.differing: F5 says code execution requires ASLR disabled or bypassed. Wiz says the HTTP/2 flaws can themselves bypass ASLR, and Rapid7's exploit leaks addresses. nginx.org rates CVE-2026-123007 only 'major' and others 'medium'; F5 scores 9.2.
sections.unknown: The extent of real-world exploitation, the share of the roughly 9 million affected services that are reachable, and distribution package fix dates are unknown. NGINX Plus R34 to R36 fix status is unclear.

items.headline: PHP announces critical security release for all supported versions on 19 November
items.summary: The PHP security team pre-announced releases for 19 Nov, 14:00–14:30 UTC, fixing CRITICAL flaws in all supported versions that need non-default or uncommon setups. Media link them to CVE-2026-115560, a session-handling RCE; details and fixed versions were not yet published.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: PHP security team announcement on php.net; reported by three outlets.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026 (php.net announcement; The Register 22:38 UTC)

sections.happened: On 18 November 2026 the PHP security team announced security releases for Thursday 19 November, 14:00–14:30 UTC, part of the four-week cycle, covering all supported PHP versions. The highest severity is CRITICAL, but the CRITICAL issues need non-default configuration or uncommon setups. This follows October's emergency PHP2Shell fixes (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), which CISA added to its KEV catalogue on 26 October according to The Register. The Register and Security Affairs link the release to CVE-2026-115560, a session-handling RCE flaw.
sections.technical: CVE-2026-115560 (media-reported link to this release) is an RCE needing all of: session.serialize_handler set to php_binary or php_serialize, code switching it to php via ini_set() before session_start(), and session upload progress enabled (the default). It is separate from PHP2Shell and not fixed by the 21 October releases (8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12). No CVSS score or fixed versions were published at time of writing.
sections.guidance: PHP's announcement urges users to prepare to upgrade promptly once releases appear. Its earlier informational advisory, as quoted by The Register, says to set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release; Hacker News adds restarting the PHP worker.
sections.unknown: Full list of CVEs, CVSS scores and fixed version numbers had not been published in the sources read. Whether CVE-2026-115560 is the CRITICAL issue is media inference.

items.headline: Ukraine arrests four suspected members of ransomware network that extorted $40.5M posing as IT support
items.summary: Ukrainian police and the FBI arrested four suspected key members of a ransomware network accused of extorting at least 28 companies of $40.5M via fake IT support calls.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Police and prosecutor announced arrests; victim details rely on court records via press.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, approx. 10:30 GMT (Censor.NET interview with acting National Police chief); Prosecutor General announcement reported Wednesday 18 Nov

sections.happened: Ukrainian National Police, with the FBI after a two-plus-year investigation, notified four key suspects of suspicion; all four are in custody. Police say at least 28 companies paid over $40.5M in ransom. Authorities say 27 members and a wider network of 60+ people in eight jurisdictions are involved. 66 searches were carried out in Kyiv and 11 regions.
sections.technical: Vector: vishing posing as IT support, with victims giving credentials or installing remote access software (MITRE T1566.004, T1219 likely; not stated by police). Stolen data was exfiltrated, files encrypted, and victims extorted for crypto. Ransomware strain not named by police; court records reportedly say Chaos.
sections.differing: Police say the $40.5M figure is paid ransom; the total damage is still being established. Court records, as reported, give the amounts for named US victims, which the police release does not.
sections.unknown: Ransomware strain officially unnamed; the link of suspects to Conti, BlackSuit or Chaos is unconfirmed; the total damage and the wider network members remain unidentified.

items.headline: ICJ rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
items.summary: The International Court of Justice found by 9 votes to 6 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. Compensation amount is deferred; Myanmar must allow safe return.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: ICJ official press release and case page; corroborated by Euronews and Semafor. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, ~09:00 UK time (ICJ reading 10:00 Hague time); first outlet report Euronews, 11:59 UK time

sections.happened: On 19 November 2026 the ICJ ruled 9-6 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State during the 2017 military campaign. It is the first time the court has found a state committed genocide. Compensation is deferred to a later phase; Myanmar must facilitate safe return and punish those responsible. The Gambia brought the case in 2019.
sections.unknown: Amount and modalities of compensation, and whether Myanmar's government will comply; the court has no enforcement power. Timing of the reparations phase is not yet set.
sections.differing: Semafor cites killing of 10,000 Rohingya; Euronews reports 'thousands' of civilians killed. Myanmar denies genocide, saying it responded to an insurgency; its representative made this case at January hearings.

items.headline: Scattered Spider-linked Scottish hacker Tyler Buchanan sentenced to six years
items.summary: Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, sentenced to 72 months in US federal prison over SMS phishing and SIM-swap crypto thefts, the fifth and final defendant sentenced.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: US Justice Department press release; sentencing reported by multiple outlets.
items.firstReported: 18 Nov 2026, 00:09 UK time (DOJ release, 17 Nov 19:09 US Eastern); first source US Attorney's Office, Central District of California

sections.happened: US District Judge John W. Holcomb sentenced Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, to 72 months on 17 November 2026. He pleaded guilty in April to wire fraud conspiracy and aggravated identity theft. He is the fifth and final defendant sentenced. A restitution hearing is set for 11 December.
sections.technical: Smishing to employees of at least a dozen companies (2021-2023) led to credential theft via phishing kit relaying logins to a Telegram channel. Stolen data enabled SIM swaps to intercept SMS two-factor codes and drain crypto wallets of over $11.6m. No CVE involved.
sections.guidance: Malwarebytes (not an authority) advises asking carriers for an account PIN or port-out lock, and using authenticator apps, passkeys or security keys instead of SMS codes.
sections.differing: Arrest date differs: Malwarebytes and SecurityAffairs say May 2024 in Palma de Mallorca; MLQ says June 2024. Loss figure rose from $8m at April plea to over $11.6m (Yahoo/Decrypt).
sections.unknown: Restitution amounts, victim identities and any further related prosecutions are not yet known. The DOJ release does not name the group.

items.headline: Ukraine strikes Crimean Bridge again; Putin vows 'much more painful' response
items.summary: Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge rail section with Neptune missiles on 19 Nov, halting trains; third strike in four days. Putin vowed a 'much more painful' response and ruled out talks.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Ukrainian MoD and Russian transport ministry both confirmed rail halt. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, 00:04 UTC per Kyiv Independent (Crimean head Aksyonov confirmed hit after midnight local time)

sections.happened: Ukrainian forces struck the Crimean Bridge on 19 Nov 2026 with Neptune missiles, hitting the rail section near the arch and tracks. Russian officials halted train traffic; no injuries reported. It was the third strike in about four days, after a 17 Nov attack collapsed a road section. Putin vowed a 'much more painful' response and said talks were off.
sections.technical: Ukraine's General Staff attributes the strike to Navy Neptune coastal missile systems. Earlier strikes reportedly used Palianytsia drones, Ruta drones and Flamingo missiles. Rail tracks and arch hit; extent of damage not yet assessed. No cyber component reported.
sections.differing: Ukraine calls the bridge a legitimate military supply artery; Putin says it is used 'exclusively for civilian purposes'. Ukraine says the strikes answer Russian attacks on its infrastructure.
sections.unknown: Extent of damage is unverified; Kyiv Independent cannot verify it. Repair timeline unclear, experts say a year or more. Dates of earlier strikes differ across outlets (16 vs 17 Nov).

items.headline: US interim rule curbs Chinese remote access to advanced AI chips; Tencent says it will slow training
items.summary: US interim rule restricts Chinese firms' remote access to advanced AI chips in overseas data centres and adds licence rules for five Southeast Asian and Brazilian destinations. Tencent says it will slow next-model training.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Rule text published by BIS; Tencent statements on earnings call; Commerce and DOJ confirmed Megaspeed probe. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026 00:39 UTC (The Register, Tencent earnings coverage); rule itself announced 16 Nov 2026 (US time)

sections.happened: Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security published an interim final rule on 16 November 2026, effective on Federal Register publication (expected 19 November). It limits remote access to advanced GPUs in non-US data centres by China-headquartered and arms-embargoed entities, and requires licences for transfers to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. Tencent's president said it would slow training.
sections.differing: Tencent's president says the rule sets China back short-term but speeds domestic chips. Singapore says it is studying the measure. China's Foreign Ministry calls it overreach (reported, not read directly).
sections.unknown: Whether H200 export clearances were rushed (The Information, unread); Megaspeed probe outcome; Senate action on RASA; effect on Tencent GPU rentals.

items.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin issue four-point 'Declaration toward Peace' after first trilateral summit in Shenzhen
items.summary: The US, Chinese and Russian leaders met in Shenzhen on 19 November and issued a four-point declaration on UN reform, energy, courts and nuclear-risk dialogue. It sets no disarmament commitments or timetable and omits Ukraine.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Declaration content reported consistently by dpa, Kyiv Post, Semafor; full text not read. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, Semafor (13:32 UK, 8:32am EST)

sections.happened: On 19 November 2026 the leaders of the US, China and Russia held their first trilateral summit in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC, lasting about 80 minutes according to Semafor. They issued a joint declaration of four points: UN reform, increased production and supply of refined petroleum products, a statement that the International Criminal Court must not abuse its jurisdiction, and a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. It states that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought.
sections.differing: The declaration is titled as a peace document, but dpa notes it contains no specific disarmament commitments or timetable and does not mention Ukraine. Semafor describes the meeting as long on symbolism but short on substance. Putin said he did not expect everything to go so well.
sections.unknown: The full declaration text was not read directly. Next steps on the nuclear dialogue, and any separate Ukraine discussions, are unclear.

items.headline: European Commission staff systems disrupted for about 10 days by cyberattack; CERT-EU involved
items.summary: Politico reports a cyber campaign took HR and medical-reimbursement systems offline at the European Commission for about 10 days. The Commission confirms targeted systems; data exposure is unconfirmed, and CERT-EU reportedly detected an AI vulnerability-scanning tool, ARTEX.
items.label: UNCONFIRMED CLAIM
items.labelBasis: Commission spokesperson acknowledged a detected cyber campaign; details rest on Politico reporting. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, morning UK time; Politico (via Reuters)

sections.happened: Politico reported on 19 November 2026 that a cyberattack hit the European Commission, disrupting some systems for around 10 days. Offline systems included HR tools for payslips and time management (Sysper) and medical reimbursements (MyPMO). Spokesperson Thomas Regnier said individual systems were targeted and those concerned were informed. An EU official said most of the attack was contained but the full damage is unclear. Technology Commissioner Henna Virkkunen briefed commissioners, and the Commission's top internal crisis body met urgently.
sections.technical: Per Politico as relayed by Cyber Security News, CERT-EU detected use of ARTEX, a publicly available AI tool that scans IT systems for weaknesses, earlier in November. The reports name no attacker, flaw or entry method, and do not say whether ARTEX enabled access or only reconnaissance. No CVEs, IOCs or ATT&CK mappings were published.
sections.differing: Reports note the Commission has not confirmed that payslip, leave or medical reimbursement data were exposed, while Politico's source said personal data may have been compromised at scale. Neither claim is independently verified.
sections.unknown: Attacker identity, initial access, whether data was accessed or stolen, number of staff affected, and how many systems remain impaired are unknown.

items.headline: Tribunal rules Home Office must acknowledge secret technical capability notice to Apple
items.summary: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the Home Office's bid to keep secret that it served Apple a technical capability notice, which could require access to encrypted data.
items.label: CONFIRMED
items.labelBasis: Multiple outlets report the ruling; judgment itself not read. Primary source not read; based on secondary reporting.
items.firstReported: 19 Nov 2026, c.13:08 UK time, City AM

sections.happened: On 19 November 2026 the Investigatory Powers Tribunal rejected the Home Office's neither-confirm-nor-deny stance and ruled it must acknowledge a technical capability notice served on Apple. The hearing was held 17 September. Apple's challenge, and a parallel Privacy International and Liberty complaint, will proceed to a substantive hearing in 2027.
sections.unknown: The notice's technical details remain secret. The lawfulness of the notice is not yet decided. Apple and the Home Office had not commented at publication.
